learning_outcomes.text: Integrate knowledge of basic chemistry with typical mechanical engineering applications, gaining a complete overview of materials for industrial engineering in relation to their chemical composition, structure, and use characteristics.
Develop the ability to choose the best material for desired applications.
Predict physical and chemical processing to be implemented on materials to modify their structure and improve properties.
Implement appropriate measures to prolong the life of the material.
Predict the controls to be carried out to verify that the materials used meet the desired characteristics.
Critically evaluate analytical data of the mechanical behavior of a material to predict its behavior in work, and interpret data from material acceptance controls.
Acquire sufficient command of technical terminology specific to chemical teaching.
Acquire the knowledge and basic skills of the discipline to independently deepen aspects of materials science applied to civil engineering in the future.

syllabus_topics: Crystal defects: defects and solid solutions
The characteristic of the amorphous state and its formation
Phase diagrams with complete solubility at the solid state, with partial solubility at the solid state (eutectic, peritectic)
Compounds with congruent and incongruent melting
Materials types: metals, polymers, composites, glasses, wood
Iron alloys: steel (carbon, stainless), cast iron
Polymeric materials: classification, properties, examples of polymeric materials (PE, PS, PVC, ABS, PET)
Composite materials, with emphasis on polymer matrix composites
Glass materials: structure, properties, fabrication and types of glass
Numerical examples related to covered topics
teaching_methods: Classroom lectures making use of the projection of transparencies
In-class numerical examples with emphasis on mechanical and thermal properties of materials, mix design and state diagrams

assessment_methods.method: Written test (six questions and two numerical exercises)

assessment_rules: Assessment will be by a written test. An oral exam is compulsory for those who achieve a grade between 18/30 and 21/30 on the written exam, while it is optional for those who achieve at least 22/30. The oral exam consists of two questions whose answers may confirm, improve, or worsen the written exam grade. The “cum laude” is awarded for achieving the highest score on each question combined with mastery of disciplinary vocabulary.
bibliography: W. D. Callister, D. G. Rethwisch, “Materiali per l’Ingegneria Civile ed Industriale”, Ed. EDISES.
